options.text: Use the Elevator
options.feedback: Very dangerous! Never use an elevator during a fire because of the risk of being trapped.

options.text: Take shelter in the lab
options.feedback: Incorrect. In a fire, the top priority is to evacuate the building immediately.

options.text: Go straight to the emergency stairs
options.narrative: The emergency door is blocked by debris and fire.

steps.instruction: Jiro hears a scream in the lower parking area of the building and sees a hysterical Siti sitting with glass shards stuck in her thigh and burns on her arm.
From the lobby emerges a student named Budi, coughing from inhaling smoke from the raging fire.
A man suddenly jumps from the top of the burning building, it's Tono from the next department.
Tono is lying there with a broken leg and severe burns. His face is covered in soot, and his breathing is hoarse and wheezing—signs of severe inhalation injury.
Prioritize aid: identify extensive burns, signs of inhalation injury, and choose the victim with the highest risk of rapid death.
What assignment do we give Budi to help Siti?

options.text: Pull out the glass shards
options.feedback: Do not pull out sharp objects — it can worsen the bleeding.

options.text: Apply a dressing and pressure to the bleeding area
options.narrative: Correct. Direct pressure and a bandage effectively stop arterial bleeding temporarily. Make sure Budi DOES NOT touch the glass, let alone pull it out.

options.text: Give her water to drink
options.feedback: Dangerous. Do not give drinks to trauma victims.

steps.instruction: Tono has many dangerous injuries, but which of his injuries is the most urgent to treat?

options.text: The severe burns all over his body
Inhalation injury that is blocking his airway
options.narrative: Tono has now stopped breathing and needs help immediately!

options.text: The fracture in Tono's leg

steps.instruction: Open the airway with a head-tilt/chin-lift because there is no neck injury, then check if air can still pass through.
The bleeding in Siti's thigh has significantly reduced. What is the best action for the arterial bleeding in Siti's thigh?

options.text: Apply a makeshift tourniquet with a belt or rope
options.feedback: Incorrect. An emergency tourniquet is a last resort. Direct pressure around the wound is much more prioritized!

options.text: Continue maintaining the dressing and pressure on the bleeding area
options.narrative: Exactly! The embedded sharp object must not be pulled out. Strong pressure around it is enough to control the arterial bleeding temporarily.

options.text: Slowly and carefully pull out the glass shards
options.feedback: Very dangerous! Pulling out the glass shards will open the natural plug of the wound and trigger fatal massive bleeding.

steps.instruction: Siti's burn is at the level of...

options.text: First degree
options.feedback: Incorrect. Siti's burn appears more severe than just mild redness.

options.text: Second degree
options.narrative: Correct. Siti's burn is more consistent with a 2nd-degree burn, thus needing cooling and proper wound covering.

options.text: Third degree
options.feedback: Does not match. The characteristic of a 3rd-degree burn is white/charred and stiff skin, which is not Siti's condition in this story.

steps.instruction: Budi offers toothpaste to apply to Siti's burn so it cools down quickly. What is your action?

options.text: Accept Budi's advice and apply toothpaste
options.feedback: Very dangerous! Toothpaste contains chemicals that can irritate the wound.

options.text: Forbid it, because household items will worsen the wound
options.narrative: A very appropriate step! Household items like toothpaste or butter will trap heat, worsen the wound condition, and make medical cleaning at the hospital later more difficult.

options.text: Apply butter because it can absorb heat
options.feedback: Wrong. Butter is fat-based and will actually trap heat inside the wound.

steps.instruction: You notice fluid-filled blisters on Siti's burn. What should you do with those blisters?

options.text: Pop them so the fluid comes out and they dry quickly
options.feedback: Wrong. Popping the blisters will open a path for bacteria and cause infection.

options.text: Leave them intact as they are
options.narrative: Exactly. Intact blisters act as a natural biological bandage that protects the wound from bacterial infection. It is strictly forbidden to pop them.

options.text: Apply ointment and press until they pop
options.feedback: Incorrect. Blisters must not be intentionally popped using any method.

steps.instruction: Siti suffered 2nd-degree burns on her arm. Cool the wound with running room-temperature water (not ice) to stop the burning process and relieve pain. Then, immediately remove a watch or jewelry around the wound before tissue swelling (edema) occurs.
Continue pouring running water on Siti's burn for 15-20 minutes or until medics arrive.
